thread:
Maya (CS): heads-up — Acme reported their quantized endpoint (prod-us-west, model v3-quant) is ~2x slower than their fp16 endpoint and outputs are slightly lower-quality. they attached logs and a short repro.
Diego (Runtime): thanks, can you paste the repro payload and their perf numbers?
Maya (CS): pasted below from customer: 
> request: 512-context, 1 prompt, streaming disabled
> fp16 p95: 210ms, quant p95: 420ms
> accuracy regressed on our eval set by ~3% (QA metric)
Maya (CS): customer says this started after we rolled the FP8/INT8 rollout last week for that pool.
Priya (ML): interesting — could be calibration stepping into a slow kernel path or kv-cache invalidation causing longer recurrent setup.
Diego (Runtime): first thought: kernel selection fallback triggered because sequence length pattern changed (longer prefixes). do we have kernel routing logs for that pool?
Ethan (SRE): deploy-bot shows recent kernel selector rule change on 1779870000: `prefer_int8_when_calibrated=true`. linking log: https://deploys.internal/r/4772
deploy-bot: rule change applied by Lia (Eng) — 1779870123
Lia (Eng): that was the config to steer model variants into int8 on dedicated pools after calibration. I didn't see e2e perf regression locally.
Diego (Runtime): can someone capture a single-request profile with `RUNTIME_PROFILE=1` for the customer's payload? need kernel name aliases (e.g., int8_kernel_v2, fp16_kernel_v5) and batch formation timeline.
Maya (CS): customer attached a small profile snippet. pasting sanitized lines: 
```
kernel_select: int8_kernel_v2
kv_init: 18ms
batch_wait: 12ms
kernel_exec: 390ms
total: 420ms
```
Priya (ML): kernel_exec 390ms is the issue. compare to fp16_kernel_v5 which should be ~180ms for same sequence. suggests int8 path is slower for their sequence length. could be a bad convolution GEMM kernel chosen for that particular seq_len and beam config.
Diego (Runtime): agree. we have heuristics that pick kernels by (model_variant, seq_len_bucket, hardware_arch). looks like the seq_len bucket boundaries are off — requests with prefix padding are routed to slower int8 kernels.
Ethan (SRE): quick mitigation options to propose to customer: 
- pin to fp16 model variant (config change, immediate)
- force kernel override to fp16 kernel for that pool (hotfix)
- temporarily disable `prefer_int8_when_calibrated` rule for Acme's pool
Maya (CS): customer asked for a non-disruptive fix first. they'll accept a pool-level override for now.
Lia (Eng): I can push a pool override to route Acme's pool to `fp16_kernel_v5` only. need confirmation on config key and approval.
Diego (Runtime): before we do that, let's reproduce locally with their exact prompt shape and batching. Maya can you share the prompt lengths distribution?
Maya (CS): customer said 95% of calls are single-turn with prompt token counts between 380-480.
Priya (ML): those are high prefixes; for int8 kernels we tuned for 0-256 and 256-1024 but performance cliff happens when attention kernel chooses blocked-matmul variant. we should add a fallback to force the fast fp16 kernel for 380-480 range.
Diego (Runtime): repro plan:
1) run bench harness with seq_len 400, batch_size=1, kv_cache enabled, kv_warmup=1
2) capture kernel logs and nvtx profile
3) try `KERNEL_HINT=fp16_kernel_v5` and `FORCE_QUANT=false` overrides

Lia (Eng): I'll schedule the override after Diego confirms the command. Maya — let the customer know we'll try a pool override in a short maintenance window and that we expect p95 to return to ~200ms.
Maya (CS): messaging drafted: "We're going to route your pool to the fp16 kernel variant temporarily while we investigate. This is non-disruptive and can be reverted any time. Expect improved latency and we'll follow up with a postmortem." ok?
Priya (ML): longer term: sounds like we need to refine kernel selection to consider effective prefix length (post-tokenization length, not raw tokens), and improve calibration profiles to record microbenchmarks per seq_len bucket. also add regression tests that compare quantized vs fp16 p95 on representative workloads.
Diego (Runtime): agreed. immediate action items:
- Diego: reproduce locally and confirm override command (timeline: 60-90m)
- Lia: stand by to apply pool kernel override once confirmed (timeline: 30m after Diego)
- Priya: run microbench for int8 kernels at seq_len 380-480 and post results to thread (timeline: 3h)
- Maya: send customer comms and schedule the maintenance window (timeline: 20m)

Ethan (SRE): monitoring checklist: add temporary alert to watch Acme p95 and error-rate for 1h after override. I'll create a pager duty rule suppressed for now.
Maya (CS): customer replied: "Thanks — can you also check output drift? we rely on QA metric." they want a post-change sample comparison.
Priya (ML): we'll run A/B sample with 1000 eval prompts across fp16 vs current quant config and share delta. I'll attach diffed outputs and aggregate QA metric.
Diego (Runtime): repro logs coming in — I can reproduce the kernel slowdown locally. forcing fp16 kernel drops kernel_exec from ~380ms -> ~185ms. nvprof trace shows int8 kernel using an unoptimized matmul tiling for this shape. attaching brief trace excerpt.
Maya (CS): lia, can you proceed with pool override now?
Lia (Eng): doing it now: `PUT /internal/pools/acme/routing` payload `{\"kernel_hint\":\"fp16_kernel_v5\",\"force_variant\":true}` 
Lia (Eng): applied — status OK 200
deploy-bot: routing override applied to pool acme by Lia (Eng) — 1779877230
Maya (CS): customer reports p95 is now ~208ms and QA metric difference reduced to 0.2%. they're happy for now.
Priya (ML): thanks. will continue microbench and propose changes to selector heuristics and calibration step to avoid this class of regression.
Diego (Runtime): I'll open a runtime ticket tracking: `RUNTIME-1325 kernel-selector: prefer_int8 causes perf cliff at high prefix lengths` and link this thread.
Maya (CS): great. closing loop with customer and will post a follow-up once kernel selector change is rolled. :thumbsup:
Ethan (SRE): adding an ephemeral grafana dashboard for Acme p95; set retention 2h.
Lia (Eng): note for postmortem: validate canary sampling includes high-prefix customers.
Priya (ML): putting a reminder to add quant vs fp16 microbench to CI harness.
Diego (Runtime): thanks everyone.
Maya (CS): thread resolved for now — will re-open if regressions reappear.
